newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banker wants leeway on EMU deficit target.
newsitem.headline: German banker wants leeway on EMU deficit target.

text.p: Martin Kohlhaussen, president of the Federal Association of German Banks, said Germany should not be preoccupied with strictly meeting Maastricht Treaty deficit criteria, a German newspaper reported.

In an interview with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Sonntagszeitung, Kohlhaussen said Germany should enter the first wave of monetary union in 1999 even if its budget deficit is as high as 3.3 percent of gross domestic product.
According to the Maastricht Treaty, nations wanting to join monetary union are to have budget deficits no larger than 3.0 percent of GDP.

Kohlhaussen, who is also chief executive at Commerzbank AG, said more important than the amount of new debt in 1997 was for Germany to have sustained budget stability in the years after the start of monetary union.
He went on to say that the recent debate between Bonn and the Bundesbank on revaluing German official reserves was unfortunate, but that it would not have a lasting impact on Germany's reputation.
